### 1. What's Life Like in This Ward?
On hot summer afternoons, the tin roofs and concrete buildings bake like an oven because our ward officially records zero trees and zero parks for shade. When it rains, even a small shower makes water pool everywhere because nearly 91% of our roads have no roadside naalas at all. For the 25,005 people living here around Bharati Vidyapeeth, daily life means sweating through sticky 34°C heat and wading through flooded lanes during the monsoon.

---

### 2. Problems and What We Can Do About Them

| Problem | How Bad Is It? | Why Does This Happen Here? | What Can Be Done? |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Street flooding (pani bharaav) | Very bad. Over 90% of our roads have no rain gutters. | Only 9.2% of roads have roadside naalas, so rainwater has nowhere to go. | Dig new side drains and clean existing naalas before heavy showers hit. |
| Extreme heat | Terrible indoors, touching over 34°C in summer. | Packed buildings and metal sheets trap heat, turning homes into hot boxes. | Put white heat-reflecting paint on rooftops to bounce away the sun. |
| No trees or shade | Severe. Officially, there are 0 trees and 0 public parks. | Every corner has been paved over with cement, leaving no green space. | Plant hardy roadside shade trees and set up small neighbourhood plant pots. |
| Dirty water & sewage | Manageable now, with 100% slum homes connected to sewer lines. | Underground pipes are present, but open gutters can still choke on plastic trash. | Clean out garbage regularly so dirty water does not back up onto streets. |
| Water shortage | A worry in dry months as ground stays parched. | Rainwater runs off paved roads into the distance instead of seeping into our soil. | Set up rooftop rainwater collection tanks to save water for daily chores. |

---

### 3. How Will the Money, Workers and Time Be Used?

| Work To Be Done | How Many? | Money (Rs.) | Workers Needed | Time Needed | Who Is Responsible? |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| White heat-reflecting paint for rooftops | 5 building clusters | Rs. 600,000 | 10 workers for a month | 1 month | PMC Building & Development Department |

- **Total money being used:** Rs. 600,000 out of Rs. 700,000
- **Money left over:** Rs. 100,000
- **Workers needed:** 10.0 person-months
- **Everything done in:** 1 months

---

### 4. What Should the Ward Officer Do? (Step by Step)

1. **Week 1:** Visit the most crowded lanes around Bharati Vidyapeeth. Pick the 5 building clusters with the hottest metal or concrete roofs and talk to the families living there.
2. **Week 2:** Buy good-quality white heat-reflecting roof paint with the PMC team and hire a local team of 10 painting workers.
3. **Week 3:** Sweep, scrub, and wash the selected roofs clean, then paint on the first thick white coat.
4. **Week 4:** Apply the final finish coat, inspect every painted roof with the residents, and safely put away the Rs. 100,000 balance for urgent drain cleaning.

---

### 5. How Will Residents Know Things Are Getting Better?

- ✅ Homes with white-painted roofs will feel noticeably cooler in the afternoon, so fans stop blowing burning-hot air.
- ✅ Families living on top floors will spend less money on electricity because they will not need coolers running all day long.
- ✅ The painted rooftops will visibly shine bright white, keeping whole lanes feeling a bit more comfortable even on dry, sunny 34°C days.
